key_findings.finding: Direct experimental evidence is the 2014 study of NDV/FMW in A549-derived drug-resistant lung cancer models: cisplatin-resistant A549/DDP cells and paclitaxel-resistant A549/PTX cells. NDV/FMW attenuated autophagy in A549/DDP but induced autophagy in A549/PTX; thus the beneficial modulation was inhibition in the former and induction in the latter, not a single uniform direction.

source_tools.relevance: Primary study abstract and results preview specify cell models, resistance phenotypes, and opposite NDV/autophagy responses.

key_findings.finding: In A549/DDP, autophagy inhibition with chloroquine (CQ), or ATG5 knockdown, enhanced NDV/FMW antitumor activity; in A549/PTX, the autophagy inducer rapamycin enhanced oncolysis. CQ and rapamycin also potentiated NDV activity in mice bearing the respective resistant tumors. Modulation did not increase viral progeny, indicating that enhanced killing was not explained by increased virus yield.

source_tools.relevance: Primary study directly reports pharmacological/genetic modulation, in vitro and mouse antitumor outcomes, and viral progeny result.
Repeated primary-study abstract confirms direction-specific treatment outcomes and unchanged virus progeny.

key_findings.finding: Mechanistic evidence includes autophagy measurements (GFP-LC3 puncta, double-membrane vesicles, and LC3-I-to-LC3-II conversion) and pathway findings: NDV/FMW-induced autophagy in A549/PTX was associated with dampening class I PI3K/Akt/mTOR/p70S6K signaling, whereas in A549/DDP infection attenuated autophagy through activation of a negative regulatory pathway. The available retrieved abstract/preview does not specify the downstream mechanism of enhanced cell killing beyond increased antitumor/oncolytic activity.

source_tools.relevance: Primary study methods and results provide autophagy assays and pathway interpretation.

key_findings.finding: The second search primarily surfaced reviews and broad NDV/autophagy discussions, not a retrieved direct experimental study in a different tumor model that tests pharmacological autophagy modulation against NDV oncolysis. Such studies should not be conflated with the direct lung-cell evidence; evidence for other models was not established in this search.
